title: Table reservation requirements
idea: Scoping a restaurant table reservation system means naming who books, seats and marks no-shows, the one rule that must never break, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Customers search free times for a party size, book, and cancel.
The host seats arriving parties and frees the table when they leave.
The core rule: one table never holds two overlapping reservations.
Assume busy evening peaks; state every number as an assumption.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: The customer gives a date, a time and a party size, and sees which start times are free.
Choosing a time books it. The system, not the customer, picks the table.
A customer can cancel before the meal, which frees the table for others.
The host seats the party on arrival and closes the reservation when they leave.

edges.label: updates
edges.caption: Seating and finishing change the reservation, so the table's schedule stays true.

edges.label: no-show
edges.caption: The system is an actor too: after a grace period it marks absent parties as no-shows.
A waitlist, paid deposits and joining tables wait for later. Say so before you design.

code.title: Scope and assumptions
code.caption: Use cases with their actor, the v1 cut, and the stated assumptions kept in one record.

walk.text: v1 is an explicit set. Anything not listed is out of scope.
Print each use case with its actor and an IN or OUT tag.
The assumptions become one object that later code can ask questions.
Three actors: the customer, the host at the door, and the system.
Waitlist, deposits and joined tables are named, so the cut is visible.
Seating length, start step, largest party and grace period, all in minutes or people.

pitfalls: Do not let customers pick a table; the system allocates it by party size.
Agree on how long a party keeps a table before designing any overlap check.
Forgetting the system actor hides the no-show rule until late in the design.

quiz.q: Which requirement shapes the reservation design the most?
options: Customers can browse the menu while booking
A table is never booked twice for overlapping times
Search results load in under 5 ms
Hosts can print a daily seating sheet
quiz.why: Two parties arriving for one table breaks the core promise. Allocation, locks and database constraints all exist to protect this one rule.

takeaway: Agree on actors, seating length and the no-overlap rule before designing.

starters: Should seating length depend on party size?
Why is joining two tables out of scope for v1?
Which scale assumptions should I state in an interview?
